paper_1.description: Objective/multiple choice paper comprising eighty questions: forty lexical and forty structural questions. Each question has four options lettered A to D.

lexis.everyday_usage: Home, social relationships, and common core school subjects.
general_vocabulary_fields: Human Internal Body system and function
lexis.idioms: Idiomatic expressions and collocations (e.g., ‘hook, line and sinker’, ‘every Tom, Dick and Harry’) whose total meaning cannot be arrived at from dictionary meanings alone.
lexis.structural_elements: Sequence of tenses, matching of pronouns with antecedents, correct use of prepositions, etc.
lexis.figurative_usage: Candidates expected to recognize when an expression is used figuratively rather than literally.

includes: Patterns of changes in word-forms which indicate number, tense, degree, etc.
Patterns in which different categories of words regularly combine to form groups and sentences.
Use of structural words e.g. conjunctions, determiners, prepositions, etc.

ghana_specific.description: Multiple choice objective paper with Parts A (lexical and structural) and B (literature).
lexis_fields: Finance – commerce, banking, stock exchange, insurance
Printing, publishing, the press and libraries
Sea, road, rail and air transport

literature.note: For Prose and Drama, study one prescribed text each.

paper_2.description: Essay, Comprehension and Summary. Duration: 2 hours. Total: 100 marks.

assessment_criteria: Content: relevance of ideas to the topic
Organization: formal features, paragraphing, emphasis and arrangement of ideas
Expression: effective control of vocabulary and sentence structure

skills_tested: Find appropriate equivalents for selected words or phrases
Identify and label grammatical structures and explain functions
Identify and explain basic literary terms
Recast phrases or sentences into grammatical alternatives
Summarize points in clear, concise English avoiding repetition

listening_comprehension.description: Sixty multiple choice questions on consonants, clusters, vowels, diphthongs, stress, intonation, dialogues and narratives.
sections: Section 1: Word final voiced/voiceless consonants and clusters
Section 2: Vowel quality in isolated words
Section 3: Vowel quality and consonant contrasts
Section 4: Vowel/consonant contrasts (sentence, isolated words, or rhymes)
Section 7: Comprehension of longer dialogues and narratives

test_of_orals.description: Sixty multiple-choice questions covering vowels, consonants/clusters, rhymes, word stress/syllable structure, emphatic stress/intonation patterns, phonetic symbols.

consonants.single: Recognize and produce significant sound contrasts (examples provided in syllabus for initial, medial, final positions).
consonants.clusters: Initial and final clusters; produce sounds in right order.

stress.word_stress: Contrast stressed/unstressed syllables; shifting stress in derivations (e.g., ‘increase vs in’crease).

notes: The syllabus varies slightly by country (especially Paper 1 and Paper 3). General vocabulary focuses on educated, non-specialist usage. Emphasis on practical application rather than rote definitions.
